sources.fullCitation: Ben Berlin und sein Orchester, with German refrain vocal. “Auf Wiederseh’n, Herr Doktor!” Fox-trot; label credit “(Rotter-Kaper).” Grammophon, elektrische Aufnahme, Katalog-Nr. B 51823, Bestell-Nr. 23042, side marked 2, label parenthetical “(W. B. W. 2)”, n.d. The uploader names Alexander Fleßburg as the refrain singer and gives 1930 as the recording year; neither is printed on the label. Shellac disc from the Schallarchiv of the Radiomuseum Hardthausen, its label filmed in the YouTube upload.

Grammophon, elektrische Aufnahme, Serie Polyfar “R” Orchester, Katalog-Nr. B 50959, Bestell-Nr. 22222, side marked 2, n.d. The uploader gives Berlin, 1929 as the recording and first release. Shellac disc from the Schallarchiv of the Radiomuseum Hardthausen, its label filmed in the YouTube upload.

sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, Refrain: Leo Moll. “Signorina aus Brioni.” Tango; label credit “Tango (Fritz Rotter und Dr. Kaper); Text: Fritz Rotter und Dr. Kaper”. Electrola, Katalog-Nr. E.G. 2400, n.d. The label also carries the B.I.E.M. mark and the designation Tanz-Orchester mit Refraingesang; the uploader identifies the refrain singer billed as Leo Moll as Leo Monosson, gives 1931 as the year of release, and illustrates the transfer with a photograph of Brioni from 1930. Shellac disc from the Schallarchiv of the Radiomuseum Hardthausen, its label filmed in the YouTube upload.
sources.title: Signorina aus Brioni — Electrola E.G. 2400
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, Refrain: Leo Moll

sources.shortCitation: Novaphon Electro Record B Nr. 4051, “Du bist verrückt, mein Schatz, du denkst an Liebe”
sources.fullCitation: Tanzorchester J. Geiger, Refraingesang: Hans Rotter. “Du bist verrückt, mein Schatz, du denkst an Liebe.” Lied und Foxtrot; label credit “Musik und Text von Fritz Rotter und Dr. B. Kaper”. Novaphon Electro Record, Katalog-Nr. B Nr. 4051, n.d. The label is marked Made in Austria and carries the B.I.E.M. mark; the matrix number beside the catalogue number is only partly legible. The uploader names the band as Tanzorchester Isy Geiger, dates the flexible disc to about 1931, and holds it in the Radiomuseum Hardthausen sound archive. Flexible disc from the Schallarchiv of the Radiomuseum Hardthausen, its label filmed in the YouTube upload.
sources.title: Du bist verrückt, mein Schatz, du denkst an Liebe — Novaphon Electro Record B Nr. 4051
sources.creator: Tanzorchester J. Geiger, Refraingesang: Hans Rotter
sources.date: n.d. [issued in Austria about 1931 according to the uploader]

sources.shortCitation: Kristall, “Ich frag', Madame, wann kommen wir zusamm'?”
sources.fullCitation: George Nettelmann und sein Orchester, Refrain: Walter Jurmann. “Ich frag', Madame, wann kommen wir zusamm'?.” Foxtrot; label credit “Bronislaw Kaper, Walter Jurmann und Fritz Rotter”. Kristall, 1931. The upload places the recording in Berlin in 1931 and names the film „Ehe m.b.H.“; the title list at musiktiteldb.de gives this Nettelmann side as Kristall 3229, recorded in Berlin on 15 September 1931. Shellac disc from the Schallarchiv of the Radiomuseum Hardthausen, its label filmed in the YouTube upload.

sources.fullCitation: Tanz-Orchester Dajos Béla, Gesang: Luigi Bernauer, auf dem Etikett als Fred Lustig angegeben. “Signorina, ich liebe dich.” Tango; label credit “Walter Jurmann, Bronislaw Kaper und Ernst Marischka”. Odeon, 1932. The upload names the film „Hochzeitsreise zu dritt“ and dates the Odeon issue to 1932, where the Odeon label list gives the coupling as O-11768 with matrix Be 10147 and places it in 1933. Shellac disc from the Schallarchiv of the Radiomuseum Hardthausen, its label filmed in the YouTube upload.
